title: Grateful Dead Live at Salt Palace on 1973-02-28

ai_review.summary: Warm but grainy soundboard captures a stellar early‑1973 set featuring smoking China > Rider, He's Gone, The Other One > Eyes > Morning Dew and an exquisite Row Jimmy.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – the China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue, the long jams on He’s Gone, Truckin’→The Other One→Eyes→Morning Dew, and a sublime Row Jimmy make this a top‑tier 1973 show. The recording is a genuine soundboard tape with noticeable hiss, occasional graininess and missing material after Eyes, but it remains listenable and warm enough to showcase the band’s tight playing and stellar vocals.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for musical performance (many 4‑5 ★ reviews) combined with mixed but acceptable recording quality yields an overall rating just above four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muffled early tracks (China Cat → The Promised Land), grainy and slightly distorted sections, audible hiss/pops between songs, missing material after Eyes, and a few seconds of dead air at the start of a track.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Truckin' > The Other One > Eyes > Morning Dew
poor_songs: Jack Straw (sound not up to par)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑1973 layout with a solid first set and a second set that builds into long, exploratory jams; transitions are praised especially the China > Rider pair and the The Other One → Eyes → Morning Dew sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals praised; guitar tone not specifically mentioned but overall performance lauded.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as powerful ("blow‑torching Jack Straw"); vocal harmonies highlighted.
band_member_comments.Bob: Singing singled out as excellent, especially in the tight vocal blend.
